handoffs.reason: Optimism Gateway is labelled a bridge, but its route is not registered in this tool, so no handoff was attempted: we do not know which chain it leads to or how its payouts appear there. The trace stops at it on ethereum rather than guessing a destination. This is a gap in our registry, not a claim that the funds did not move.
handoffs.inference_note: This is an inference, not an observation. The deposit is recorded on chain; the arrival of the same value on the destination chain is matched by amount, timing and destination address, and no public data links the two transactions.

cross_chain.note: A cross-chain handoff is an inference, not an observation. The deposit is on record on its own chain; the arrival of the same value on the destination chain is matched by amount, timing, recipient address and payout contract. It carries its own score, which is never merged into the on-chain confidence figure.

typologies.name: Rapid pass-through
typologies.explanation: 0x036587e7…5654f9 received 1,220 ETH and forwarded 1,220 ETH of it - 99% - holding the funds for a median of 79 seconds, with the whole movement in and out completed inside 4 hours. A wallet that keeps nothing and forwards almost immediately is acting as a conduit rather than as a destination, so the funds' owner is more likely to be found further along the chain than here. This says nothing about who operates the wallet; automated forwarding services behave the same way.

typologies.name: Structuring (split into equal parts)
typologies.explanation: 0xf7b31119…5cf1be sent ETH to 7 different wallets in amounts that are all close to 3,003 ETH - they vary by only 0.0% around that figure. Amounts that uniform are chosen, not incidental: value is being deliberately broken into equal parts, which is done to keep individual transfers below a reporting or monitoring threshold and to spread them across accounts. Regular scheduled payments of a fixed size can look identical, and this wallet is not a labelled business, so the purpose of the payments is not established here.

typologies.name: Round-value transfers
typologies.explanation: 30 of the 30 ETH transfers out of 0x0dcb08ea…2df8b2 are flat round figures (100 ETH). Amounts like these are chosen rather than computed, which fits value being moved to order rather than paid for goods or services. On its own this means very little - round transfers are entirely normal - and it is recorded here only as corroboration for the other pattern(s) found on these wallets.

typology_summary.scope: Only wallets the FIFO taint pass attributed suspect funds to are described, so patterns in unrelated traffic through the same wallets are not reported.
typology_summary.caveat: Typologies are patterns in the transfer graph, not conclusions about intent. Each is a reason to investigate further and states the measurements and thresholds that produced it so they can be challenged. Legitimate automated activity can reproduce every pattern here, and strength is never reported as certainty.
typology_summary.thresholds_note: Thresholds are deliberately strict: a wrongly asserted typology in a police report is more damaging than a missed one. All of them are configurable - see the typology settings in config.py.

accounting.rule_label: FIFO (first in, first out): funds leave a wallet in the order they arrived.
accounting.rule_detail: Amounts attributed to the suspect are computed by replaying every observed transfer in chronological order and drawing each outgoing payment from the front of the wallet's queue of received funds. Ties are broken by block, then transaction index, then transaction hash. Value a wallet sent that its observed inflows cannot account for is treated as untainted. A different accounting rule - last-in-first-out, or pro-rata pooling - would produce different figures from the same transactions.
accounting.assumed_pre_existing_note: Summed across every wallet in the trace, not the uncertainty on any one finding. A wallet that spent more than the inflows we observed must have held funds from before the observation window; that shortfall is treated as untainted, which understates taint rather than inventing it. For the figure that applies to a specific finding, see path_assumed_pre_existing on that finding.
accounting.tie_break_rule: timestamp, then block number, then transaction index, then transaction hash
accounting.tie_broken_value_note: Value moved by transfers the blockchain does not order relative to a sibling touching the same wallet and asset - same timestamp, block and transaction index - where our hash comparison chose the order. An upper bound on what the convention could have affected, not an error estimate: in most such ties the outcome is the same either way.
